# Doctiling

> AI knowledge base for teams, free to start with no credit card. Experts curate your sources; AI agents answer from them and cite every claim.

What Doctiling is: A knowledge management system. Your information lives in knowledge bases you govern — one per client, team or case — with documents, tables and graphs, its own system prompt, its own tools and its own permissions. Your experts curate that content and AI agents analyse it, compare it and turn it into tables, charts, diagrams and code, always citing where each claim came from. The base is shared with your team, published or connected over MCP to the tools you already use.

Who it is for: AI for legal teams that cites the exact clause; An AI knowledge base for consulting firms; Healthcare AI that answers from your own sources; AI for finance teams where every figure is cited; AI for literature reviews with citations you can verify; A shared knowledge base for engineering teams and their coding agents.

Access: Free access is sponsored and invitation-only. Request a demo with your email; once we approve it you can sign in and use the full studio — knowledge bases, document editor, AI agent with citations, mirror view, custom tools — with a sponsored AI budget and a quota of 50 AI calls per day. No credit card, no trial clock. Upgrade only if you need isolation or higher volume. Self-hosting: With a usage license, one command installs the full studio on your infrastructure. Point it at a local model and work without third parties.

Every page exists in English (/en/) and Spanish (/es/).

# English

## AI knowledge base for teams | Doctiling

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/landing

AI knowledge base for teams, free to start with no credit card. Experts curate your sources; AI agents answer from them and cite every claim.

**What exactly is Doctiling?**

A knowledge management system. Your information lives in knowledge bases you govern — one per client, team or case — with documents, tables and graphs, its own system prompt, its own tools and its own permissions. Your experts curate that content and AI agents analyse it, compare it and turn it into tables, charts, diagrams and code, always citing where each claim came from. The base is shared with your team, published or connected over MCP to the tools you already use.

**Is it a document manager or a vector search engine?**

Neither, although it does what both do. It stores your sources with permissions and indexes them by meaning, but that is where its work starts: structuring them into documents, tables and graphs, letting your experts curate them — edit, validate, retire what is stale — and having AI agents analyse them with citations. What you get is not a file found, but verified knowledge you can reuse, share and query from other tools.

**How is this different from a generic AI chat?**

Generic chats answer from memory and sometimes invent. Doctiling indexes every block of your documents and retrieves the relevant passages before answering, so every claim ships with a citation back to your own content. If it's not in your sources, the agent says so instead of guessing.

**Does this replace the RAG project we were going to build in-house?**

For most cases, yes. Chunking, embedding, the vector index and citation are already built and tested; you need no pipeline of your own and nobody to maintain it. What stays in your hands is what actually decides the outcome: which sources enter each base, who has access, which tools the agent may call and which systems query it. If your case demands full control of the stack, the self-hosted build runs the same product on your infrastructure.

**Who can see my documents?**

Only you and the people you explicitly invite, under roles (owner, admin, collaborator, reader). On the Free plan your data is logically isolated per user; Gold moves you to your own dedicated database, and Platinum adds dedicated infrastructure on top.

**How do I get free access?**

Free access is sponsored and invitation-only. Request a demo with your email; once we approve it you can sign in and use the full studio — knowledge bases, document editor, AI agent with citations, mirror view, custom tools — with a sponsored AI budget and a quota of 50 AI calls per day. No credit card, no trial clock. Upgrade only if you need isolation or higher volume.

**How much does Doctiling cost?**

It depends on whether you are a person or a company. A person pays for their account in the shared studio: about USD 28 a month on Basic, USD 82 on Advanced or USD 233 on Max, all included (COP 91,000, COP 268,000 or COP 763,000). A company pays from about USD 15 a month (COP 49,000) for its private studio, plus each person’s plan: Basic about USD 24, Advanced USD 78 or Max USD 229 (COP 77,900, COP 254,900 or COP 749,900). Each plan comes with an AI balance in pesos (about USD 21, USD 69 or USD 207 a month, enough for about 150, 500 or 1,500 queries); if it runs out, you top up from about USD 6 (COP 20,000) and get that same amount as balance. If the company connects its own AI, the plan drops to about USD 3, USD 9 or USD 22 (COP 9,800, COP 29,400 or COP 71,900). There is also free access by invitation and a license to run it on your infrastructure. You are charged in Colombian pesos, at fixed prices, before taxes; USD figures are a reference.

**What is a query, and what happens when they run out?**

A query is one request to the AI: a question to the agent, a generated document, a scheduled task or a search in your documents. Your plan does not come with a fixed number of queries but with an AI balance in pesos, and each query takes what it cost: simple ones take little, big ones more. If the balance runs out, AI pauses until the 1st or you top up from about USD 6 (COP 20,000); the rest of the studio keeps working.

**How do I pay, and can I cancel?**

You are invoiced every month in pesos and charged automatically to the payment method you register. You can pay the year up front and get two months free, and cancel whenever you want, with no penalty; we keep your information for 60 days.

**What is MCP and why should I care?**

Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets external AI tools read from a data source. With Doctiling you can expose a knowledge base through a scoped, revocable, read-only token, so the desktop AI tools your team already uses can query your documents as a source of truth.

**Does it work in Spanish?**

Yes — the whole studio is bilingual (Spanish and English) and you can switch at any moment. The agent reads and answers in the language of your documents and your questions.

## AI for legal teams that cites the exact clause

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/use-cases/legal

Doctiling is a knowledge base for legal teams: you upload the matter file, ask in plain language and the AI agent answers citing the document and the page each statement comes from. If something is not in your documents, it says so instead of inventing it.

From those answers it drafts briefs, timelines and clause-comparison tables, every line traceable to its source, so the work can be defended to a client or a judge.

Reviewing contracts and building a case theory means re-reading hundreds of pages without missing the clause that changes everything. Generic AI chats summarize well but can invent citations — and a fabricated citation in a filing is a professional liability.

Each matter gets its own knowledge base with its own permissions. The agent retrieves the relevant passages before answering and attaches the citation, so you check the clause in one click instead of trusting a summary.

**Can the AI invent a legal citation?**

Doctiling retrieves passages from your own documents before answering and attaches the citation to each claim. If the answer is not in your sources, the agent says so instead of guessing.

**Are my clients' files mixed with other firms' data?**

No. Only the people you invite can see a knowledge base, under roles (owner, admin, collaborator, reader). On the Gold plan your data lives in its own dedicated database.

**Can we deliver the work under our own brand?**

Yes. The Gold plan includes custom domain and white-label branding.

**Does it work with documents in Spanish?**

Yes. The studio is bilingual (Spanish and English) and the agent answers in the language of your documents and your questions.

## An AI knowledge base for consulting firms

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/use-cases/consulting

Doctiling gives each engagement its own knowledge base: you centralize the data room, interview transcripts and client documents, and an AI agent synthesizes them into deliverables where every conclusion cites the document it came from.

The client sees the trail behind each finding, and your team can query the same knowledge base from the tools it already uses, over MCP.

A project starts with hundreds of client documents, transcripts and data rooms. Turning all of that into a clear, defensible deliverable is where billable time goes — and the client wants to see the trail, not a black box.

Mirror view stacks summaries, entity tables, mind maps and correlations beside each document. Every finding can be saved as a variant, so you compare approaches without losing where each one came from.

**Can I keep each client's information separate?**

Yes. Each knowledge base has its own documents, permissions, system prompt and tools; you create one per client, team or case.

**How does the client know where a conclusion comes from?**

Every claim the agent makes ships with a citation to the document and section in the knowledge base, so the trail is visible in the deliverable.

**Can my team use it from the tools they already have?**

Yes. A knowledge base can be exposed through MCP with a scoped, revocable, read-only token, so other AI tools your team uses can query it as a source of truth.

**Does this replace building our own RAG?**

For most cases, yes: chunking, embedding, the vector index and citation are already built. You decide which sources enter each base and who has access.

## Healthcare AI that answers from your own sources

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/use-cases/healthcare

Doctiling is a knowledge base for healthcare teams: you bring together clinical guidelines, literature and notes, and the AI agent answers clinical questions citing the source of each statement. If something is not in your documents, it says so — it does not invent a dose or a finding.

It summarizes follow-ups and cross-checks a finding against the evidence you loaded, so the time goes to care instead of searching.

Patient information lives scattered across notes, labs and clinical guidelines. Finding a history or cross-checking a finding against the literature eats the time that should go to care, and an assistant that invents a dose is unacceptable.

The agent works only from the sources in the knowledge base and shows where each answer comes from. Access is limited to the people you invite, with roles, and paid plans move your data to a dedicated database or dedicated infrastructure.

**What happens if the answer is not in our documents?**

The agent says so instead of guessing. Every claim it makes ships with a citation back to your own content.

**Who can see the information?**

Only the people you explicitly invite, under roles. On the Free plan data is logically isolated per user; Gold moves you to a dedicated database and Platinum adds dedicated infrastructure.

**Can we run it on our own infrastructure?**

Yes. The self-hosted build runs the same product on your infrastructure.

**Does it replace clinical judgement?**

No. Doctiling retrieves and cites what your sources say; the decision stays with the professional, who can check every citation.

## AI for finance teams where every figure is cited

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/use-cases/finance

Doctiling is a knowledge base for finance teams: you upload filings, statements and reports, and the AI agent produces ratio analysis, executive summaries and period-over-period comparisons where every figure links to the exact statement it came from.

An untraced number cannot be audited; here each one keeps its source, beside the document in mirror view.

Analyzing reports, computing ratios and tracking a portfolio means jumping between endless PDFs and spreadsheets. An untraced number is a number you can't audit — or defend to an investment committee.

PDF tables are rebuilt as table documents the agent can aggregate and compare, and every result cites the source. Analyses stack beside the document in mirror view, and each knowledge base keeps its own permissions.

**Can the agent work with tables from PDFs?**

Yes. Doctiling rebuilds PDF tables into table documents, which the agent can query and aggregate with citations.

**How do I verify a figure?**

Every figure in an answer links to the statement and section it came from in your knowledge base.

**Is sensitive financial information isolated?**

Only invited people see a knowledge base, under roles. Gold gives you a dedicated database and Platinum adds dedicated infrastructure.

**How do I get access?**

Free access is sponsored and invitation-only: request it with your email and, once approved, you use the full studio with no credit card.

## AI for literature reviews with citations you can verify

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/use-cases/research

Doctiling turns your corpus of papers into a knowledge base an AI agent can synthesize: it compares sources, surfaces contradictions and extracts methods and results, citing your own documents instead of producing references that do not exist.

You draft in English or Spanish and save each synthesis as a variant, so you can compare approaches without losing the trail.

A literature review is weeks of reading, annotating and cross-referencing. AI chats speed it up but can fabricate references that don't exist — poison for a thesis or a paper.

The agent answers only from the papers you loaded and cites each one. Graph documents map how concepts and authors relate, and the agent can draw diagrams and mind maps from them.

**Does it make up references?**

The agent answers from the papers in your knowledge base and cites them. If the answer is not in your sources, it says so instead of guessing.

**Can I write in Spanish from papers in English?**

Yes. The studio is bilingual and the agent reads and answers in the language of your documents and your questions.

**Can I compare different syntheses?**

Yes. Each synthesis can be saved as a variant beside the document, so approaches stay side by side with their trail.

**Is there a free option?**

Free access is sponsored and invitation-only, with a daily AI quota and no credit card.

## A shared knowledge base for engineering teams and their coding agents

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/use-cases/engineering-teams

Doctiling gathers your team's specs, architecture decisions and runbooks in a knowledge base that people ask in the studio and coding agents query over MCP. Every answer cites the document it came from, so an agent works from your decisions instead of guessing them.

Access goes through a scoped, revocable, read-only token, and the self-hosted build runs the same product on your infrastructure.

Engineering knowledge is spread across wikis, repositories and threads. New people ask the same questions, and coding agents fill the gaps with assumptions that contradict decisions the team already made.

Curate the documents that define how you build into one knowledge base and expose it over MCP. A terminal agent, a team chat or an internal system query it and get cited answers; graph documents describe how components relate.

**What is MCP and why does it matter for coding agents?**

Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets external AI tools read from a data source. Doctiling exposes a knowledge base through it, so your agents query your documents as a source of truth.

**Can we revoke an agent's access?**

Yes. Access goes through a scoped, revocable, read-only token per knowledge base.

**Can we self-host it?**

Yes. The self-hosted build runs the same product on your own infrastructure.

**Can the agent produce diagrams or code from our documents?**

Yes. Beyond cited answers, the agent produces tables, charts, diagrams and code from the content of the knowledge base.

## Doctiling vs Notion AI

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/compare/notion-ai

Choose Notion AI if your team already writes and plans in Notion and wants AI inside those pages. Choose Doctiling if you need a dedicated knowledge base built from your own sources — documents, tables and graphs — that experts curate and you can also run on your own infrastructure under a usage license.

Both answer with citations and both connect over MCP; the difference is where the knowledge lives and who governs it.

| Criterion | Doctiling | Notion AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | Knowledge bases you govern — one per client, team or case — built from your sources, curated by experts and worked by AI agents. | AI built into the Notion workspace: pages, docs, tasks and databases. ([source](https://www.notion.com/product/ai)) |
| Cited answers | Yes: every claim cites the block of the source document; if it is not in your sources, the agent says so. | Yes: answers with citations. ([source](https://www.notion.com/product/ai)) |
| Tables and graphs | Text, table and graph documents; the agent draws charts, diagrams and mind maps from them. | Databases with AI autofill; graphs not stated. ([source](https://www.notion.com/product/ai)) |
| Where knowledge comes from | File uploads and read-only SQL engines. No native sync with Google Drive, Slack or Confluence. | Search across Slack, Google Drive, GitHub and more; full Enterprise Search (beta) from the Business plan. ([source](https://www.notion.com/product/ai)) |
| MCP | Yes: each knowledge base can be exposed with a scoped, revocable, read-only token. | Yes: Notion MCP connects AI apps to the workspace. ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-mcp)) |
| Self-hosting | Yes: the same product on your infrastructure, under a usage license with public installers (the code is private). | Not stated on its official site. ([source](https://www.notion.com/pricing)) |
| Free plan | Yes: sponsored seat by invitation with AI included (50 AI calls per day), no credit card. | Free plan with a limited AI trial; full AI from the Business plan. ([source](https://www.notion.com/pricing)) |
| Pricing | Free by invitation and self-hosted under a usage license. One person, from about USD 28 a month all included (COP 91,000); a company, from about USD 15 a month (COP 49,000) for its private studio plus each person’s plan, from about USD 24 (COP 77,900) with AI included or USD 3 (COP 9,800) with its own AI. Charged in Colombian pesos. | Published: Free, Plus, Business and Enterprise plans. ([source](https://www.notion.com/pricing)) |

Notion AI data comes only from its official pages, linked next to each cell and checked on 2026-11-13. If something has changed, write to support@doctiling.app and we will correct it.

**Is Doctiling an alternative to Notion AI?**

For a knowledge base built from your own sources and curated by experts, yes. For writing and planning inside Notion pages, Notion AI is designed for that and the two can coexist.

**Do both cite their sources?**

Yes. Notion AI states that its answers come with citations; Doctiling cites the block of the source document behind each claim and says so when the answer is not in your sources.

**Can I try Doctiling for free?**

Yes. The hosted seat is sponsored and invitation-only, with AI included and no credit card.

## Doctiling vs Guru

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/compare/guru

Choose Guru if you want a governed, company-wide knowledge layer with ready connectors to tools like Slack, Google Drive or Confluence, under a sales-led contract. Choose Doctiling if you want knowledge bases per client, team or case built from documents you bring, with table and graph documents and a free way to start hosted, or self-hosted under a license.

Both cite every answer and expose knowledge over MCP; Guru connects to where knowledge already lives, Doctiling structures what you bring into it.

| Criterion | Doctiling | Guru |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | Knowledge bases you govern — one per client, team or case — built from your sources, curated by experts and worked by AI agents. | A governed knowledge layer that structures and improves company knowledge for enterprise AI. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/)) |
| Cited answers | Yes: every claim cites the block of the source document; if it is not in your sources, the agent says so. | Yes: citations on every answer. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/)) |
| Tables and graphs | Text, table and graph documents; the agent draws charts, diagrams and mind maps from them. | Not stated on its official site. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/)) |
| Where knowledge comes from | File uploads and read-only SQL engines. No native sync with Google Drive, Slack or Confluence. | Yes: integrations with Google Drive, Confluence, Slack, Notion and more. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/integrations)) |
| MCP | Yes: each knowledge base can be exposed with a scoped, revocable, read-only token. | Yes: a Guru MCP server for AI tools. ([source](https://help.getguru.com/docs/connecting-gurus-mcp-server)) |
| Self-hosting | Yes: the same product on your infrastructure, under a usage license with public installers (the code is private). | Not stated on its official site. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/)) |
| Free plan | Yes: sponsored seat by invitation with AI included (50 AI calls per day), no credit card. | Not stated; reduced cost for eligible nonprofits. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/pricing)) |
| Pricing | Free by invitation and self-hosted under a usage license. One person, from about USD 28 a month all included (COP 91,000); a company, from about USD 15 a month (COP 49,000) for its private studio plus each person’s plan, from about USD 24 (COP 77,900) with AI included or USD 3 (COP 9,800) with its own AI. Charged in Colombian pesos. | Not published: custom package through sales. ([source](https://www.getguru.com/pricing)) |

Guru data comes only from its official pages, linked next to each cell and checked on 2026-11-13. If something has changed, write to support@doctiling.app and we will correct it.

Not as a native source sync: you upload files or connect a read-only SQL engine. In the other direction, a Slack bot or Teams app can consume the knowledge base through its MCP endpoint.

## How to build an AI knowledge base for your team

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/guides/ai-knowledge-base

An AI knowledge base is the set of sources your team decides to trust — contracts, manuals, reports, decisions — organised so an AI agent answers from them and cites where every claim comes from. Building one well depends less on technology than on four decisions: what goes in, how it is structured, who curates it and where it is queried from.

### Start with one process, not every document

The most common mistake is uploading the whole shared drive and expecting the AI to make sense of it. A base with everything answers with everything: old versions, drafts and documents that contradict each other.

Pick one concrete process — answering questions about a master agreement, preparing a committee, handling support questions — and build a base just for it. In Doctiling every knowledge base has its own sources, its own system prompt, its tools and its permissions, so a second process is a second base, not one more folder inside the first.

### Choose the sources that actually answer the question

For each base, make a short list: which documents would an expert use to answer the questions of that process. That list is the base. Everything else can be added later, when a real question calls for it.

PDF, Word, spreadsheets, web pages and notes all work. What matters is that they are the current version and that someone can say "this is correct". If two documents contradict each other, decide which one rules before uploading them, or retire the one that is out of date.

### Structure: text, tables and graphs

Not all knowledge is prose. A contract is read clause by clause; a price list or a financial statement is a table; a map of systems or stakeholders is a graph of relationships.

Doctiling keeps all three as documents of the same base: text is cut into blocks at headings, PDF tables are rebuilt as queryable tables and graphs are queried by neighbourhood. So the agent can cite the exact clause, add up a column or follow a relationship, instead of guessing from plain text.

### Curation: the step that separates a useful base from an archive

Indexing documents is the easy part. What makes a base trustworthy is someone with judgement maintaining it: fixing what was badly converted, validating what is used to decide and retiring what no longer applies.

Give each base an owner and time for that job. With roles (owner, admin, contributor, reader) you decide who can change the content and who only queries it. Every agent answer cites the block it came from, so errors show up and are fixed at the source, not in the answer.

### Querying: in the studio, in the team chat or over MCP

A base pays off when people use it where they already work. In the Doctiling studio you talk to the agent, which answers with citations and produces tables, charts, diagrams or new documents from the base.

Outside the studio, the same base can be exposed over MCP with a scoped, revocable, read-only token, so a desktop AI tool, a coding agent or an internal system can query it as a source of truth. Start with one base and a small group; grow when real questions show what is missing.

**How is an AI knowledge base different from a generic AI chat?**

A generic chat answers from what it learned in training and can make things up. An AI knowledge base first retrieves passages from your own sources and answers from them, citing every claim. If the answer is not in your sources, the agent says so.

**How many documents do I need to start?**

Few. A useful base can start with the ten or twenty documents an expert would use to answer the questions of one process. A small, current base beats a large, messy one.

**Do I need a technical team to build it?**

No. In Doctiling chunking, indexing and citation are already built: you upload the sources, organise them and curate them from the studio. What you do need is someone who knows the subject and decides what goes in and what comes out.

## What MCP is and how to connect your knowledge base

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/guides/what-is-mcp

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets an AI tool — a desktop assistant, a coding agent, a chat — connect to an external data source and query it while it works. Connecting your knowledge base over MCP makes those tools answer from your documents, not from what they remember.

### The problem MCP solves

Every AI tool your team uses knows a lot about the world and nothing about your company: it does not know your contracts, your architecture decisions or your procedures. Until recently, giving it that context meant copying and pasting, or building a custom integration for each tool.

MCP defines a common way to do it. A data source is exposed once as an MCP server and any compatible client can query it, with no custom integrations.

### How it works, in plain terms

There are two pieces. The MCP server exposes tools — for example "search this base" or "read this document" — and describes what each one does. The MCP client is the AI tool: it reads those descriptions and decides when to call them to answer what it is asked.

The client does not get a copy of your data. It asks for what it needs for each question and the server decides what to return, based on the permissions of the token it connected with.

### What changes when the source is a curated base

Connecting a folder of files over MCP gives the tool access to everything, drafts and old versions included. Connecting a curated knowledge base gives it access only to what your team has validated.

In Doctiling, a base's MCP endpoint returns passages with their citation: the source document and section. The tool asking can show that citation, and whoever reads the answer can check it.

### Security: scoped, revocable tokens

MCP access in Doctiling goes through a read-only token, scoped to one knowledge base and revocable at any time. A token for the engineering team's coding agent does not open the legal team's base.

If a tool is no longer used or someone leaves the team, you revoke their token and access ends. For organisations with strict requirements, the self-hosted version runs the same product on their own infrastructure.

### How to connect it, step by step

First, build and curate the base you want to expose: only what should be a source of truth. Second, create an MCP token for that base from the studio. Third, add the endpoint URL and the token to the settings of the tool that will query it; most compatible clients have a section for MCP servers.

From then on, when you ask something the base answers, the tool will query it and bring back the answer with its citation. Review from time to time which tokens are still active.

**Does MCP belong to a particular AI vendor?**

No. It is an open standard implemented by several desktop AI tools, coding agents and platforms. A base exposed over MCP serves any compatible client.

**Can the connected tool modify my base?**

No. In Doctiling the MCP token is read-only: the tool queries and gets cited answers, but it does not edit or delete content.

**How is MCP different from an API?**

An API is called by a program written for it. MCP is used by an AI tool that reads the description of each operation and decides on its own when to call it. That is why connecting a base over MCP needs no code on the client side.

## RAG vs a curated knowledge base: what changes in the answers

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/en/guides/rag-vs-curated-knowledge-base

RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) is the technique: find relevant passages in your documents and hand them to the model before it answers. A curated knowledge base is what feeds that technique. RAG decides how to search; curation decides what is worth finding.

### What RAG does

A RAG system cuts documents into chunks, indexes them by meaning and, for each question, retrieves the most similar chunks and gives them to the model along with the question. The model answers from those chunks instead of only from memory.

It is the basis of almost every assistant that answers from your own documents, and it greatly reduces made-up answers. But RAG retrieves what it finds: if what it finds is outdated or contradictory, so is the answer.

### Where RAG over uncurated documents fails

Three failures keep coming back. First: versions. The index holds the 2023 policy and the 2025 one, and the system retrieves whichever looks most like the question, not the current one. Second: lost structure. A PDF table flattened to plain text mixes rows and columns, and the model reads figures that do not belong together. Third: noise. Drafts, emails and duplicates compete with the documents that matter.

None of these failures is fixed by a better model. They are fixed at the source.

### What a curated knowledge base adds

Curating means deciding what goes in, in what form and who answers for it. In practice: one current version of each document, tables that stay tables, relationships kept as a graph and a person who retires what is obsolete.

On top of that base, retrieval works with reliable material. Doctiling combines search by meaning and by keyword over blocks cut at headings, and every answer cites the exact block, so an error can be traced back to its source and fixed there.

### Build your own RAG or use a managed base

Running an in-house RAG takes a conversion pipeline, chunking, embeddings, a vector index, citation, permissions and someone to maintain it all. It makes sense when you need full control of every piece.

For most teams the value is elsewhere: in which sources go into each base, who has access and from which tools it is queried. A managed base like Doctiling ships that pipeline built and leaves those decisions in your hands. If everything must run on your infrastructure, there is a self-hosted version.

### How to tell whether your system needs curation

Ask ten real questions from your process and check the citations of each answer. If they point to expired documents, drafts or the wrong section, the problem is not retrieval: it is the base.

Start with the process that gets the most repeated questions, keep only what is current in the base, give it an owner and ask the same ten questions again. The difference between the two rounds is what curation brings.

**Does a curated knowledge base replace RAG?**

No, it complements it. RAG is the technique of retrieving passages before answering; the curated base is the material it works on. Doctiling runs retrieval over a base your team curates.

**Why does my RAG assistant cite old documents?**

Because it retrieves the chunk that looks most like the question, not the most recent one. If the index holds several versions of a document, it can bring back any of them. The fix is to keep only the current version in the base.

**Does curating a base take a lot of time?**

Less than correcting wrong answers. Start with a small base for one process, one owner and a periodic review of what goes in and out. The citations on every answer show where curation is needed.

Un sistema de gestión del conocimiento. Tus expertos curan ese contenido y agentes de IA lo analizan, comparan y convierten en tablas, gráficas, diagramas y código, citando siempre de dónde salió cada afirmación. La base se comparte con tu equipo, se publica o se conecta por MCP a las herramientas que ya usas.

**¿Es un gestor documental o un buscador vectorial?**

Ninguno de los dos, aunque hace lo que ambos hacen. Guarda tus fuentes con permisos y las indexa por significado, pero su trabajo empieza ahí: estructurarlas en documentos, tablas y grafos, que tus expertos las curen — editar, validar, retirar lo obsoleto — y que agentes de IA las analicen con citas. **¿En qué se diferencia de un chat de IA genérico?**

Los chats genéricos responden de memoria y a veces inventan. Doctiling indexa cada bloque de tus documentos y recupera los pasajes relevantes antes de responder, así cada afirmación llega con una cita a tu propio contenido. Si no está en tus fuentes, el agente lo dice en vez de adivinar.

**¿Reemplaza el proyecto de RAG que iba a montar internamente?**

Para la mayoría de los casos, sí. El troceado, el embedding, el índice vectorial y la citación ya están construidos y probados; no necesitas un pipeline propio ni alguien manteniéndolo. Lo que queda en tus manos es lo que de verdad decide el resultado: qué fuentes entran a cada base, quién tiene acceso, qué herramientas puede usar el agente y desde qué sistemas se consulta. Si tu caso exige control total del stack, la versión autoalojada corre el mismo producto en tu infraestructura.

**¿Cómo obtengo el acceso gratis?**

El acceso gratis es patrocinado y por invitación. Solicita una demo con tu correo; cuando lo aprobemos podrás iniciar sesión y usar el estudio completo — bases de conocimiento, editor de documentos, agente IA con citas, vista espejo, herramientas propias — con un presupuesto de IA patrocinado y una cuota de 50 llamadas IA al día. Sin tarjeta, sin reloj de prueba. Pasa a un plan pago solo si necesitas aislamiento o más volumen.

**¿Cuánto cuesta Doctiling?**

Depende de si eres una persona o una empresa. Una persona paga su cuenta en el estudio compartido: $91.000 al mes en el plan Básico, $268.000 en Avanzado o $763.000 en Máximo, todo incluido. Una empresa paga desde $49.000 al mes por su estudio privado, más el plan de cada persona: Básico $77.900, Avanzado $254.900 o Máximo $749.900. Cada plan trae un saldo de IA en pesos ($68.100, $225.500 o $678.000 al mes, que rinde cerca de 150, 500 o 1.500 consultas); si se gasta, recargas desde $20.000 y ese mismo valor queda de saldo. Si la empresa conecta su propia IA, el plan baja a $9.800, $29.400 o $71.900. También hay acceso gratis por invitación y una licencia para correrlo en tu infraestructura. **¿Qué es una consulta y qué pasa si se acaban?**

Una consulta es una petición a la IA: una pregunta al agente, un documento generado, una tarea programada o la búsqueda en tus documentos. Tu plan no trae un número fijo de consultas sino un saldo de IA en pesos, y cada consulta descuenta lo que costó: las sencillas gastan poco y las grandes, más. Si el saldo se acaba, la IA se pausa hasta el día 1 o recargas desde $20.000; el resto del estudio sigue funcionando.

**¿Qué es MCP y por qué debería importarme?**

Model Context Protocol es un estándar abierto que permite a herramientas de IA externas leer una fuente de datos. Con Doctiling puedes exponer una base de conocimiento mediante un token acotado, revocable y de solo lectura, para que las herramientas de IA de escritorio que tu equipo ya usa consulten tus documentos como fuente de verdad.

**¿Funciona en español?**

Sí — todo el estudio es bilingüe (español e inglés) y puedes cambiar de idioma en cualquier momento. El agente lee y responde en el idioma de tus documentos y de tus preguntas.

Doctiling reúne las specs, decisiones de arquitectura y runbooks de tu equipo en una base de conocimiento que las personas consultan en el estudio y los agentes de código consultan por MCP. Cada respuesta cita el documento de donde salió, así un agente trabaja con tus decisiones en lugar de adivinarlas.

El acceso pasa por un token acotado, revocable y de solo lectura, y la versión self-hosted corre el mismo producto en tu infraestructura.

El conocimiento de ingeniería está repartido entre wikis, repositorios e hilos. Las personas nuevas hacen las mismas preguntas, y los agentes de código llenan los vacíos con supuestos que contradicen decisiones que el equipo ya tomó.

Cura en una base de conocimiento los documentos que definen cómo construyen y exponla por MCP. Un agente de terminal, un chat de equipo o un sistema interno la consultan y reciben respuestas citadas; los documentos de grafo describen cómo se relacionan los componentes.

**¿Qué es MCP y por qué importa para los agentes de código?**

Model Context Protocol es un estándar abierto que permite a herramientas de IA externas leer de una fuente de datos. Doctiling expone una base de conocimiento por ahí, así tus agentes consultan tus documentos como fuente de verdad.

**¿Podemos revocar el acceso de un agente?**

Sí. El acceso pasa por un token acotado, revocable y de solo lectura por base de conocimiento.

**¿Podemos alojarlo nosotros mismos?**

Sí. La versión self-hosted corre el mismo producto en tu propia infraestructura.

**¿El agente puede producir diagramas o código a partir de nuestros documentos?**

Sí. Además de respuestas citadas, el agente produce tablas, gráficas, diagramas y código a partir del contenido de la base de conocimiento.

## Cómo armar una base de conocimiento con IA para tu equipo

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/es/guides/ai-knowledge-base

Una base de conocimiento con IA es el conjunto de fuentes que tu equipo decide confiar — contratos, manuales, informes, decisiones — organizado para que un agente de IA responda desde ellas y cite de dónde sale cada afirmación. Armarla bien depende menos de la tecnología que de cuatro decisiones: qué entra, cómo se estructura, quién la cura y desde dónde se consulta.

### Empieza por un proceso, no por todos los documentos

El error más común es subir la carpeta compartida completa y esperar que la IA la entienda. Una base con todo responde con todo: versiones viejas, borradores y documentos que se contradicen.

Elige un proceso concreto — responder dudas de un contrato marco, preparar un comité, atender preguntas de soporte — y arma una base solo para él. En Doctiling cada base de conocimiento tiene sus propias fuentes, su propio system prompt, sus herramientas y sus permisos, así que un segundo proceso es una segunda base, no una carpeta más dentro de la primera.

### Elige las fuentes que de verdad responden la pregunta

Para cada base, haz una lista corta: qué documentos usaría una persona experta para responder las preguntas de ese proceso. Esa lista es la base. Lo demás se puede agregar después, cuando una pregunta real lo pida.

PDF, Word, hojas de cálculo, páginas web y notas sirven. Lo que importa es que sean la versión vigente y que alguien pueda decir "esto es correcto". Si dos documentos se contradicen, decide cuál manda antes de subirlos, o retira el que quedó obsoleto.

### Estructura: texto, tablas y grafos

No todo el conocimiento es prosa. Un contrato se lee por cláusulas; una lista de precios o un estado financiero es una tabla; un mapa de sistemas o de partes interesadas es un grafo de relaciones.

Doctiling guarda las tres formas como documentos de la misma base: el texto se corta en bloques por encabezado, las tablas de un PDF se reconstruyen como tablas consultables y los grafos se consultan por vecindad. Así el agente puede citar la cláusula exacta, sumar una columna o seguir una relación, en lugar de adivinar a partir de texto plano.

### Curaduría: el paso que separa una base útil de un archivo

Indexar documentos es la parte fácil. Lo que hace confiable una base es que alguien con criterio la mantenga: edita lo que quedó mal convertido, valida lo que se usa para decidir y retira lo que ya no aplica.

Asigna una persona dueña por base y dale tiempo para esa tarea. Con roles (propietario, admin, colaborador, lector) decides quién puede cambiar el contenido y quién solo consulta. Cada respuesta del agente cita el bloque de donde salió, así los errores se ven y se corrigen en la fuente, no en la respuesta.

### Consulta: en el estudio, en el chat del equipo o por MCP

Una base sirve cuando la gente la usa donde ya trabaja. En el estudio de Doctiling se conversa con el agente, que responde con citas y produce tablas, gráficas, diagramas o documentos nuevos a partir de la base.

Fuera del estudio, la misma base se puede exponer por MCP con un token acotado, revocable y de solo lectura, para que una herramienta de IA de escritorio, un agente de código o un sistema interno la consulten como fuente de verdad. Empieza con una base y un grupo pequeño; amplía cuando las preguntas reales muestren qué falta.

**¿Qué diferencia hay entre una base de conocimiento con IA y un chat de IA genérico?**

Un chat genérico responde con lo que aprendió en su entrenamiento y puede inventar. Una base de conocimiento con IA recupera primero los pasajes de tus propias fuentes y responde desde ellos, citando cada afirmación. Si la respuesta no está en tus fuentes, el agente lo dice.

**¿Cuántos documentos necesito para empezar?**

Pocos. Una base útil puede empezar con los diez o veinte documentos que una persona experta usaría para responder las preguntas de un proceso. Es mejor una base pequeña y vigente que una grande y desordenada.

**¿Necesito un equipo técnico para armarla?**

No. En Doctiling el troceado, el índice y la citación ya están construidos: subes las fuentes, las organizas y las curas desde el estudio. Lo que sí necesitas es una persona que conozca el tema y decida qué entra y qué sale.

## Qué es MCP y cómo conectar tu base de conocimiento

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/es/guides/what-is-mcp

MCP (Model Context Protocol) es un estándar abierto que permite a una herramienta de IA — un asistente de escritorio, un agente de código, un chat — conectarse a una fuente de datos externa y consultarla mientras trabaja. Conectar tu base de conocimiento por MCP hace que esas herramientas respondan con tus documentos, no con lo que recuerdan.

### El problema que resuelve MCP

Cada herramienta de IA que usa tu equipo sabe mucho del mundo y nada de tu empresa: no conoce tus contratos, tus decisiones de arquitectura ni tus procedimientos. Hasta hace poco, darle ese contexto significaba copiar y pegar, o construir una integración a medida para cada herramienta.

MCP define una forma común de hacerlo. Una fuente de datos se expone una vez como servidor MCP y cualquier cliente compatible puede consultarla, sin integraciones a medida.

### Cómo funciona, en términos simples

Hay dos piezas. El servidor MCP expone herramientas — por ejemplo, "buscar en esta base" o "leer este documento" — y describe qué hace cada una. El cliente MCP es la herramienta de IA: lee esas descripciones y decide cuándo llamarlas para responder lo que le preguntan.

El cliente no recibe una copia de tus datos. Pide lo que necesita para cada pregunta y el servidor decide qué devolver según los permisos del token con el que se conectó.

### Qué cambia cuando la fuente es una base curada

Conectar una carpeta de archivos por MCP le da a la herramienta acceso a todo, incluidos borradores y versiones viejas. Conectar una base de conocimiento curada le da acceso solo a lo que tu equipo validó.

En Doctiling, el endpoint MCP de una base devuelve pasajes con su cita: documento y sección de origen. La herramienta que pregunta puede mostrar esa cita, y quien lee la respuesta puede verificarla.

### Seguridad: tokens acotados y revocables

El acceso por MCP en Doctiling pasa por un token de solo lectura, acotado a una base de conocimiento y revocable en cualquier momento. Un token para el agente de código del equipo de ingeniería no abre la base del área legal.

Si una herramienta deja de usarse o una persona sale del equipo, revocas su token y el acceso termina. Para organizaciones con requisitos estrictos, la versión self-hosted corre el mismo producto en su propia infraestructura.

### Cómo conectarla, paso a paso

Primero, arma y cura la base que quieres exponer: solo lo que debe ser fuente de verdad. Segundo, crea desde el estudio un token MCP para esa base. Tercero, agrega la URL del endpoint y el token en la configuración de la herramienta que lo va a consultar; la mayoría de los clientes compatibles tiene un apartado para servidores MCP.

Desde ahí, cuando preguntes algo que la base responde, la herramienta la consultará y traerá la respuesta con su cita. Revisa cada cierto tiempo qué tokens siguen activos.

**¿MCP es de un proveedor de IA en particular?**

No. Es un estándar abierto y lo implementan varias herramientas de IA de escritorio, agentes de código y plataformas. Una base expuesta por MCP sirve a cualquier cliente compatible.

**¿La herramienta conectada puede modificar mi base?**

No. En Doctiling el token MCP es de solo lectura: la herramienta consulta y recibe respuestas citadas, pero no edita ni borra contenido.

**¿Qué diferencia hay entre MCP y una API?**

Una API la llama un programa escrito para ella. MCP la usa una herramienta de IA que lee la descripción de cada operación y decide sola cuándo llamarla. Por eso conectar una base por MCP no exige escribir código en el cliente.

## RAG vs base de conocimiento curada: qué cambia en las respuestas

URL: https://www.doctiling.app/es/guides/rag-vs-curated-knowledge-base

RAG (generación aumentada por recuperación) es la técnica: buscar pasajes relevantes en tus documentos y dárselos al modelo antes de que responda. Una base de conocimiento curada es lo que alimenta esa técnica. RAG decide cómo se busca; la curaduría decide qué vale la pena encontrar.

### Qué hace RAG

Un sistema RAG corta los documentos en fragmentos, los indexa por significado y, ante cada pregunta, recupera los fragmentos más parecidos y se los entrega al modelo junto con la pregunta. El modelo responde desde esos fragmentos en vez de solo desde su memoria.

Es la base de casi cualquier asistente que responde con documentos propios, y reduce mucho las respuestas inventadas. Pero RAG recupera lo que encuentra: si lo que encuentra está desactualizado o es contradictorio, la respuesta también lo estará.

### Dónde falla un RAG sobre documentos sin curar

Tres fallas se repiten. La primera: versiones. El índice tiene la política de 2023 y la de 2025, y el sistema recupera la que más se parece a la pregunta, no la vigente. La segunda: estructura perdida. Una tabla de un PDF convertida a texto plano mezcla filas y columnas, y el modelo lee cifras que no van juntas. La tercera: ruido. Borradores, correos y duplicados compiten con los documentos que sí importan.

Ninguna de estas fallas se arregla con un mejor modelo. Se arreglan en la fuente.

### Qué agrega una base de conocimiento curada

Curar es decidir qué entra, en qué forma y quién responde por ello. En la práctica: una versión vigente de cada documento, tablas que siguen siendo tablas, relaciones guardadas como grafo y una persona que retira lo obsoleto.

Sobre esa base, la recuperación trabaja con material confiable. Doctiling combina búsqueda por significado y por palabras clave sobre bloques cortados por encabezado, y cada respuesta cita el bloque exacto, así un error se rastrea hasta su fuente y se corrige ahí.

### Construir tu propio RAG o usar una base gestionada

Montar un RAG interno exige un pipeline de conversión, troceado, embeddings, índice vectorial, citación, permisos y alguien que lo mantenga. Tiene sentido cuando necesitas control total de cada pieza.

Para la mayoría de los equipos, el valor está en otra parte: en qué fuentes entran a cada base, quién tiene acceso y desde qué herramientas se consulta. Una base gestionada como Doctiling trae ese pipeline construido y deja en tus manos esas decisiones. Si necesitas que todo corra en tu infraestructura, existe la versión self-hosted.

### Cómo saber si tu sistema necesita curaduría

Haz diez preguntas reales de tu proceso y revisa las citas de cada respuesta. Si las citas apuntan a documentos vencidos, a borradores o a la sección equivocada, el problema no es la recuperación: es la base.

Empieza por el proceso con más preguntas repetidas, deja en la base solo lo vigente, asigna una persona dueña y vuelve a hacer las mismas diez preguntas. La diferencia entre las dos rondas es lo que aporta la curaduría.

**¿Una base de conocimiento curada reemplaza a RAG?**

No, lo complementa. RAG es la técnica de recuperar pasajes antes de responder; la base curada es el material sobre el que trabaja. Doctiling usa recuperación sobre una base que tu equipo cura.

**¿Por qué mi asistente con RAG cita documentos viejos?**

Porque recupera el fragmento que más se parece a la pregunta, no el más reciente. Si el índice tiene varias versiones de un documento, puede traer cualquiera. La solución es dejar en la base solo la versión vigente.

**¿Curar una base toma mucho tiempo?**

Menos que corregir respuestas equivocadas. Empieza con una base pequeña para un proceso, una persona dueña y una revisión periódica de lo que entra y sale. Las citas de cada respuesta muestran dónde hace falta curar.
